title: Redundant Connection
summary: A connected undirected graph has one more edge than a tree on the same vertices.

contractDetails.constraints: 3–1000 vertices labeled from 1. The input has exactly n distinct edges [a,b] with 1 ≤ a < b ≤ n. The graph is connected.

statement: A connected undirected graph has one more edge than a tree on the same vertices. Return the last input edge whose removal leaves a tree. Return its endpoints as shown in the input.

examples.explanation: The fourth edge closes the cycle.
The final edge attaches a leaf. The preceding edge closes the cycle.
All three edges can be removed individually, so choose the last.

constraints: 3–1000 vertices labeled from 1. The input has exactly n distinct edges [a,b] with 1 ≤ a < b ≤ n. The graph is connected.
hints: Conceptual: Removing any edge on the one cycle breaks it.
Directional: Process edges in input order, maintaining connected groups.
Implementation: Return the edge whose endpoints are already in one group. Earlier cycle edges have already been added.
complexityAnalysis: O(V α(V)) time and O(V) space with Union-Find.
